$comment: How AFC-B meets owner rules R55 to R61 (2026-09-17). Read by ~/.claude/skills/security-rules/scripts/check-security.mjs. Stack: Django + DRF on MySQL, one database role, access decided in views. Rule text: ~/.claude/OWNER-RULES.md section D; the mapping table is in WEBSITE/CLAUDE.md.

rls.na: MySQL through one Django role: the database has no row-level security to declare. Every row a handler touches is scoped in the view (validate_token for the session, org_can_event / _is_event_admin / role gates for who may act, canonical_profile for the user's own row). The runtime proof of that scoping is security/idor-cases.json.

allow.reason: the public rankings ladders: the flagged line is the season resolver for reads that are public by design (owner rule R25); publishing is gated per season by rankings_published / tiers_published, checked by the reads themselves
the public transfer feed (/teams transfers tab): public by design, team_id only narrows a public list; writes to TeamTransfer happen elsewhere behind the team gates
payload is the OAuth state the server signed and consumed once (state.consume); the user_id in it was written by us before the provider round trip, never sent by the client
the one **create is duplicate_event copying the model's OWN columns (duplicate_field_values(source), the contract's inverted duplication); the request body only names the source event
fields is a dict this code builds by hand (user_id, phone, direction, body...) from a signature-verified Meta webhook; no request key reaches the ORM unnamed
token here is a signed back-channel logout JWT (RFC 8417 security event) posted to the partner; it is not a cookie and never reaches a browser
a helper, not a handler: device_from_request reads one token off the sign-in body for the callers (login, two-factor verify), which authenticate first; its write (remember) runs after a passed factor
public read-only endpoints (the rankings ladders, allowed under R58); the only .update( in the file is a dict; month and season are parsed with try/except and a code
the file is decoded as text in memory and parsed line by line, never stored; capped at MAX_LOG_BYTES (25 MB) since 2026-09-18; no content type is trustworthy for a game client's .log
the system f-string interpolates a staff-maintained knowledge file (load_knowledge) and a constant invite link; the admin's text goes in the user message

the cap is per ORGANIZATION: Organization.ocr_free_reads_left, decremented and refunded in afc_ocr/services/extract.py (SharedCredentials); past it the organizer's own key pays (key_required_response)

the upload goes through require_image_upload (afc_auth/image_utils.py, 2026-09-18): Pillow decodes the BYTES and verifies them, the format must be JPEG / PNG / WEBP / GIF / HEIF, 10 MB cap, refused with a code, then re-encoded by normalize_image_upload; proven both ways in afc_auth/tests_image_upload_gate.py. The gate lives in one module, which is why this file shows no check of its own

the organizer payout bank account: Paystack needs the account number readable to create a transfer recipient, so it cannot be hashed and is not encrypted today. A recorded decision, not an oversight (WEBSITE/CLAUDE.md, R63 row, 2026-09-18) and carried in the security debt ledger as MEDIUM; revisit with a Fernet field if payouts ever stop needing the raw value

https.enforcedBy: nginx on the VPS (deploy/vps/nginx-afc.conf): port 80 answers 301 to https for both hosts; HSTS max-age=31536000 includeSubDomains on both 443 server blocks
